newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh to hold peace talks with tribal rebels.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh to hold peace talks with tribal rebels.

text.p: Peace talks between the Bangladesh government and tribal rebels fighting for autonomy of the Chittagong Hill Tracts in the country's southeast resume in Dhaka on Monday.

"All preparations for the crucial meeting between the government and the Parbatya Chattagram Janasanghati Samity (PCJSS), political wing of the Shanti Bahini guerrillas, have been completed," Mohammad Ismail, deputy commissioner of Khagrachhari hill district, told Reuters on Sunday.
"The PCJSS delegation, led by Jyotirindra Budhipriya Larma, has already arrived at Dudukchhari (a rebel post near the border with northeast India's Tripura state)," he said by telephone.
They will be flown to Dhaka early on Monday.
Chief Whip of Bangladesh parliament, Abul Hasnat Abdullah, will lead a nine-member government team at the talks, aimed at signing a long-awaited treaty to end the 23-year-old tribal insurgency.

Officials said broad outlines of the treaty had already been agreed at talks between the two sides in May, but the PCJSS was facing opposition from a group of Shanti Bahini hardliners and the Hill Students Council, which backs the insurgency.

Shanti Bahini beagn the insurgency in 1973 over demands for autonomy for the 5,500 sq-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts bordering India and Burma, and expulsion of some 500,000 Bengali-speaking settlers from the region.
Over 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the protracted bush war, which also forced some 50,000 tribespeople to flee to Tripura.
Nearly 7,000 refugees returned home in March and April following an agreement between Dhaka and New Delhi, but when the second phase of repatriation would start remains uncertain, officials said.
